alternatives_considered.approach: Store a per-membership balance column updated on every expense/payment write
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Violates the project invariant that balances are derived by one recompute path and never stored; a stored column can drift from the ledger and needs its own locking, while recompute in-request is already budgeted for groups up to 200 members (TR-9 non-functional note)

alternatives_considered.approach: Exact-minimum settlement search instead of greedy min-cash-flow
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Minimum-transfer settlement is NP-complete (subset-sum); ADR-0005 already decided greedy min-cash-flow with the at-most-N-1 guarantee, and the issue contract names that algorithm explicitly

alternatives_considered.approach: Restrict settle-up endpoints to current members only and leave departed seats unsettleable
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A leave-at-zero followed by an expense edit or delete touching the departed seat strands a non-zero net no payment could ever clear, breaking the issue's own promise that the group reads all-zero; letting a current member record with a departed ledger participant of the same group keeps every net settleable without touching expense code

alternatives_considered.approach: Null payload on payment activity rows like every other non-edit kind
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The schema comment's null-payload rule assumes the linked row survives, but payment-deleted rows outlive their payment through set-null, so with nothing stored the later feed ticket could never render them; a small amount/endpoints snapshot is the minimum that keeps TR-10 renderable

work_order.approach: Add migration 0005 with a payments ledger table plus a nullable payment_id on activity_event (mirroring expense_id's set-null pattern so payment-deleted rows outlive the delete), and give payment rows a small snapshot payload (amount plus both endpoint ids and display names) so the later feed ticket can render them. Add lib/settle/: balances.ts with computeNetBalances(db, groupId) as the single recompute path (paid parts minus computed shares plus payments received minus payments sent, integer minor units, keyed by membership id with snapshotted display names, including departed seats whose membership row is deleted so nets stay truthful and sum to zero), simplify.ts with the ADR-0005 greedy max-debtor-vs-max-creditor pass with deterministic displayName/membershipId tiebreaks, validation.ts with zod boundaries for create/delete payment input, and actions.ts with createPayment/deletePayment Server Actions through guardGroup (membership check first, archived groups refuse writes, inputs validated at the boundary, each write plus its activity row in one interactive transaction). createPayment requires both endpoints to belong to the guarded group — a current membership or a departed ledger participant of that group, never an id from another group — and from != to; deletePayment requires the acting current member to be the payer or the recipient. Replace the sync getMemberBalance stub in lib/groups/members.ts with an async db-backed read through computeNetBalances and update its four call sites plus the existing mocks. Render the group debts card with per-member nets (departed holders labelled), the simplified transfer list with Settle-up buttons hidden when archived, and the settled/owes-summary banner (debts card above expenses in DOM order so narrow screens stack correctly); render home viewer totals and per-person rows under the same-currency-sum rule with an exclusion note naming foreign-currency groups, plus per-group balances in group currency read sequentially in one request. Client islands (components/settle-panels.tsx) follow the groups-panels ConfirmStep plus StateMessage (role=status, aria-live=polite) pattern: settle-up and delete-payment forms with explicit confirms, input preserved on error, in-place updates announced through the live region — no new toast infrastructure. Payment activity rows use kinds payment-created/payment-deleted with the snapshot payload for the later activity-feed ticket to render; activity feed UI itself stays out of scope.

work_order.debate_summary: The critique was a summary-only verdict of flawed with eight claims and I verified each against the code rather than applying them. Blocking (home per-person rows missing while AC-2 claims IAC-2): confirmed — the issue text, ui.md Home regions, spec tabs, TR-9 and IAC-2 all require per-person rows and the proposal's acceptance, files and qa_script omit them; fixed by extending AC-2, app/page.tsx and qa_script. Major (departed seat stranded non-zero after a later expense edit/delete, unreachable all-zero under a current-members-only rule): confirmed — removal deletes the membership row while ledger split lines keep the seat (the expense path's resolveNames previous-snapshot case proves it), so the state is reachable; fixed with the departed-ledger-participant rule plus AC-8 and tests, not by touching expense code. Major (null-payload payment rows can never render after set-null): confirmed as a specification gap — fixed by defining the snapshot payload plus AC-7 and tests, keeping feed UI out of scope. Major (endpoints not scoped to the guarded group, no cross-group test): confirmed as a precision gap against removeMember's own this-group scoping precedent — fixed in the actions rule, AC-5 and tests. Minor (cross-currency rule untested): confirmed — covered now in AC-2 and qa_script. Minor (toasts do not exist, aria-live unspecified): confirmed in the narrow sense — groups-panels has ConfirmStep plus a StateMessage live region but no toast component, so the plan now names that mechanism instead. Minor (debts card not conditioned on archived): confirmed omission — settle controls now hide when archived, matching the page's existing pattern. Minor (one computeNetBalances call per group on a single-connection backend): judged a non-defect — sequential reads in one request are correct on PGlite and within the TR-9 recompute budget, so it is recorded as a residual risk rather than a plan change. Nothing in the critique contradicts the brief's recorded decisions, so nothing was dismissed on those grounds.

issue_snapshot.title: Balances with simplified debts and settle-up payments
issue_snapshot.body:
Members can see who owes whom with at most N-1 simplified transfers and record settle-up payments until the group reads all-zero.

Person sees: group debts card with Settle-up buttons, balance banner (settled or owes-summary), home totals cards (you-are-owed, you-owe), per-person rows and group list with per-group balances. Contract: CONSUMES the expense and payment ledger; DEFINES lib/settle net balances plus greedy min-cash-flow simplification and Payment writes and deletes as ledger entries, never balance edits. Constraints: TR-9 with at most N-1 transfers, balances derived by one recompute path and never stored, involved-member-only payment delete.

**Risk.** Money-trust risk: balances derived by one recompute path and never stored, greedy min-cash-flow capped at N-1 transfers, payments as ledger entries with involved-member-only delete.

**Out of scope**
- Activity feed UI
- Seed data and deploy guide
- Moving money in the app (settle-up only records payments, per spec)

Covers: TR-3, TR-9, TR-11
Part of #1.
Depends on #6.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Group page shows per-member net balances plus simplified who-pays-whom with at most N-1 transfers via the stated greedy min-cash-flow, with an explicit settled and all-zero state
- **IAC-2** Home shows cross-group you-owe and you-are-owed totals per person alongside per-group balances
- **IAC-3** Record full and partial settle-up payments from the debts card with a confirm, delete them as an involved member with a confirm, and see balances update in place with an aria-live announcement
- **IAC-4** Amounts render in the group currency from one formatter with tabular numerals; the debts card sits above expenses on narrow screens

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:12:18.702Z):
  Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:25:43.988Z):
  All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.
